title.en: Data Quality, Labelling and Pipelines for Analysis
title.ar: جودة البيانات والوسم ومسارات إعدادها للتحليل

tagline: REPLACE: one line under the title: what participants can do after the course
description: Participants build the data an analysis depends on for Bayyin Consumer Protection Office, a fictional regulator holding 30,000 synthetic complaint records in Arabic and English. They write a labelling guideline, pilot it, measure agreement and adjudicate, run golden-question checks and review queues across a rater team, turn analysts' requirements into quality rules and a data contract, and package the preparation as a reproducible pipeline that stops on those rules. Measuring model-made labels is DS-306; platform-scale data engineering is AE-306.
audience: Practitioners. Data scientists and analysts who have completed the level 200 set or can show equivalent work: an analysis they framed, carried out and explained to a stakeholder.
prerequisites: DS-202 Data Acquisition, Preparation and Quality
FN-102 Command Line, Git and Reproducible Projects
Writes Python functions and SQL queries
Uses Git and a lock-file environment

outcomes.text: Draft a labelling guideline with definitions, decision rules and edge cases, and revise it after a pilot, given 300 synthetic complaints labelled by three raters
outcomes.evidence: a versioned guideline whose change log ties each revision to a measured disagreement

outcomes.text: Compute chance-corrected agreement by category and rater, and adjudicate the disagreements, given two rounds of pilot labels
outcomes.evidence: an agreement report with intervals and an adjudicated set

outcomes.text: Configure a labelling workflow with golden-question checks, review queues and rater-drift monitoring, given a simulated round of 2,000 items from six raters, one of whom drifts
outcomes.evidence: a quality-control report that flags the drifting rater and states cost per accepted label

outcomes.text: Implement quality rules with thresholds and severities, and a data contract for the prepared table, given four source tables with seeded defects
outcomes.evidence: rules and a contract that catch each defect and reject a breaking schema change

outcomes.text: Build a reproducible preparation pipeline from raw extracts to an analysis-ready table that stops on a blocking rule, given a repository with continuous integration
outcomes.evidence: run logs that pass on clean data and fail on a seeded defect from a clean checkout

outcomes.text: Diagnose why an analytical figure changed after a data refresh and decide on the correction, given two runs, their lineage records and a stakeholder asking which figure is right
outcomes.evidence: an incident note with root cause, affected outputs and correction
